title: Review of c02's FCH chemoton (SIBE): S, I and B replicate on fresh seed 13; at the feed-cut fork the vesicle shrinks to a small ring but does not die by t=600, so E is not seen as death. Weak
summary: I looked at pack/seed0/sheet.png and starve_fork.png, then re-ran world.py and world_starve.py (feed cut at t=300, otherwise identical) on seed 13 with labkit. Fed: from the noisy bath a catalyst-bearing body forms by t~81 and becomes a double-walled vesicle with K beaded on its outer bilayer by t~183; it keeps its size to t=600 (labkit persistent area ratio 1.11; radial K rim/core 6.53, rim/out 1.91). A second, K-free multilamellar body shrinks to a small ring and persists on amphiphile from the bath, as the claim notes for seed 1. Starved twin: after t=300 the K vesicle loses its outer wall and shrinks to a ring about a third of its diameter that is still present at t=600, while the amphiphile total falls 90% (FACTS channel drift -0.90). The body depends on the feed, but within the run it shrinks rather than dies, so the E gate's 'individuals die' is not met on this seed.

observations.S: rerun/seed13/sheet.png t=0: noisy bath, no structure
observations.I: rerun/seed13/sheet.png t=183-600: one K-bearing double-walled vesicle at constant size (FACTS persistent area ratio 1.11)
observations.B: rerun/seed13/FACTS.md: radial catalyst K rim/core 6.53, rim/outside 1.91, peak rho 1.15

seeds_run.result: pass for S, I, B; E fork: shrink without death by t=600

controls_run.E: rerun/starve13 (feed cut at t=300, same seed): the K vesicle shrinks to a small ring that persists to t=600; amphiphile total -90%

verdicts.limitation: One fresh seed holding only one K-bearing vesicle; the fork ends at t=600, so the shrunken ring may die later; E holds by construction (amphiphile only from K and P) and I saw shrinkage, not death. No resolution test.
